verdict_rules.reference: Chrome's default fingerprint (branded Chrome, fresh profile, no flags; includes ca34)
verdict_rules.exact: 0 counted fields differ from Chrome's default fingerprint
verdict_rules.exact_variant: 0 counted fields differ from one of Chrome's less common variants (without ca34, or the post-quantum experiment), but not the default
verdict_rules.close: exactly 1 counted field differs from the default fingerprint
verdict_rules.behind: 2 or more counted fields differ from the default fingerprint
verdict_rules.versions_behind: Chrome major of the newest fully rolled-out stable (per platform, latest.json current_stable.highest_full_rollout) minus the major in the profile name

caveats: Chrome sends more than one real fingerprint. The default (branded Chrome 156.0.8078.47, fresh profile, no flags) includes the trust-anchors extension ca34; --disable-features=TLSTrustAnchorIDs removes it; and 6% of linux stable clients are in Google's PqcBandwidthExperiment, which adds extension 0x12e0. Every library is compared against all three; the verdict uses the default.
Reference: branded Google Chrome 156.0.8078.47 (stable), captured Oct 22, 2026 on Linux x86_64 against a local capture server (capture/lib/server.py).
No population figure exists in the capture for Chrome without ca34 (no Finch study in the seed toggles it), so none is shown.
HTTP/3: 8 library profiles were tested over QUIC against the same local aioquic endpoint that captured Chrome's QUIC fingerprint; libraries without an HTTP/3 client are marked 'no HTTP/3 support'.

Resumption, extension-order shuffling and header order come from the behaviour probe (leaderboard/harness/probe.py): 8 requests per row on one client against our local capture server, which closes each connection, with the browser's captured header set passed in the browser's order. Header order counts toward the verdict only where the exact header set arrived in the same order on every request.
Verdicts compare against the Linux Chrome capture. Windows and macOS and Android Chrome are captured separately and shown next to Linux; libraries are not scored against them.
